title: Email
description: Transactional email: a Mailer service on Cloudflare Email Service, printed to the console in development, plus invitation emails with organizations.

envVars.name: MAIL_FROM
envVars.description: Sender address; its domain must be enabled for Cloudflare Email Sending (wrangler email sending enable <domain>)

envVars.name: MAIL_TRANSPORT
envVars.description: cloudflare (default) sends through the EMAIL binding; console prints emails instead (the local value)

guide.purpose: Send invitations, receipts and password resets. Call `send` on the `Mailer` service. In production the layer sends through Cloudflare Email Service; in development (`MAIL_TRANSPORT=console`) it prints each message to the dev server log. With organizations, invitations are emailed too.
guide.swap: `MailerLive` already chooses between two implementations by `MAIL_TRANSPORT`. To add a provider, write another layer for `Mailer` in `apps/web/src/server/mailer.ts` and return it from `MailerLive` for a new `MAIL_TRANSPORT` value.

args.name: mailTransport

args.content:
## Email

- Send mail through the `Mailer` service from `@repo/core` (`send({ to, subject, text, html? })`); do not use the `EMAIL` binding directly. Always send a `text` body.
- `apps/web/src/server/mailer.ts` picks the transport from `MAIL_TRANSPORT`: `console` (the local value in `.env.example`) prints the message to the dev server log, anything else sends through Cloudflare Email Service with the `EMAIL` `send_email` binding. `MAIL_FROM` must be an address on a domain enabled for sending: `wrangler email sending enable <domain>`.
- Transactional mail only (invitations, receipts, password resets); use a dedicated platform for marketing or bulk sends.

### Invitation emails

- `organization({ sendInvitationEmail })` in `auth.ts` calls `invitation-email.ts`, which emails the `/accept-invite/<id>` link through the `Mailer`. A failed send is logged and does not fail the invitation; the link is still shown to the inviter.
